result:
I've made the card-pick sheet offer and accept only cards the reached Core effect actually takes, without changing Core's resolution, fallback or explicit Auto. Nothing was compiled or run; author execution is **NOT_RUN**. Core stayed read-only, and the edits are limited to the five allowed files.

**Why the old sheet was wrong:** Core's `TakePick` quietly discards a manual pick its effect won't take and uses its own fallback instead (`Battle.PlayerActions.cs:260-275`). Each authored pick card has exactly one pick effect, and no earlier effect on any of them changes whether a visible card is eligible. The one real exception is costdown right after Rien's ultimate (more on that below).

**Production change**
- **One shared filter for all three paths:** the drawn sheet, `PickCard` acceptance and the waiting-intent re-check all go through the same function now. The waiting intent also re-checks its frozen effect list.
- **`PickCandidates`** keeps its old signature and gains two optional parameters (the effect rule and a cost lookup). Old callers compile unchanged and still get the old zone list.
- **New public helpers:**
  - `ChoiceRules`: which Core effect each pick request feeds.
  - `EffectEligible`: a copy of Core's own check per effect. tune skips rarity C and cards already carrying the part. costdown uses Core's real `BattleCostOf`, with no cost arithmetic of mine. recall skips rarity C. growPick needs growth below 3. copyPick now includes evolutions of a growth card, which the old filter missed.
  - `PickBlocked`: offers nothing when Core would skip the effect (growth cap, full hand), or when the cost can't be known yet.
- **Empty sheet:** it now says why it's empty. Explicit Auto is unchanged.

**Gap that needs a Core decision (not built):** with exactly one free-card charge left (after Rien's ultimate plus one play), playing the card spends the charge before costdown runs. The current cost query returns 0 for every card, so the client can't tell which cards will be eligible. For now the sheet blocks manual picks in that one case and leaves Auto to Core. A pure Core query, e.g. `Run.BattlePickEligible`, would close it; details are in report §5.

**Tests (all NOT_RUN)**
- **`EffectCandidatePlayModeTests`**, three client tests using only APIs the old client already had:
  - `TuneSheetOffersAndAcceptsOnlyCardsItsCoreEffectTakes`: should fail on old Main.
  - `ExplicitAutoStillSendsCoresOwnChoiceAndNeverAHiddenCard`: its list check should also fail on old Main.
  - `APreparedTunePickUsesTheSameEligibleList`: should fail on old Main.
  - They rely on one test-local fixture, restored in finally: the source's only rarity-C cards are curses, so one hand card's definition is set to rarity C in both the client's and the mirror's content. The task's example of a "common card" doesn't work as a witness: `com_slash` and `com_guard` are rarity B, so they're eligible.
- **`EffectCandidateCoreWitnessTests`**, seven pure tests on real content:
  - `ChoiceRules` maps all 14 authored pick cards.
  - tune skips the real `eye_of_rift` curse, and a card already tuned in an earlier turn.
  - costdown follows real costs, including the `c_lite` part and a reserve-only card.
  - costdown under Rien's free cards: exact with two charges left, blocked with one (where Core does take the card).
  - recall skips the curse, while exhaustPick still takes any discard card.
  - growPick excludes growth 3 and blocks at the battle cap.
  - copyPick offers the evolved card, and its free copy fails costdown.
  - Each one compares the client function with Core's own result on a twin battle.
- **Old-Main RED run:** drop the `EffectCandidateCoreWitnessTests` class (the middle block of the file); it uses the new API. The two adapted files below use no new API.
- **Adapted:** the PickerGuard sheet test now expects the filtered list (the old zone-helper check is kept). The PreparedIntent `Tune` witness now also requires a card tune can actually take.

**Risks**
- **Non-owned tests:** `ExpeditionClientPlayModeTests.PickSheetForecasts…` and the TurnFlow stale-sheet test assume every hand card is offered. They would fail only if their seed-1234 hand holds a curse or an already-tuned card at that moment; if so, they need the same narrowing as PickerGuard.
- **Uncovered branches:** these are listed honestly in report §7, e.g. the full-hand recall block, which can't be reached with authored cards, and hidden draws that happen when a card is played.

Next on your side: review, capture RED on old Main, then the targeted and full PlayMode/EditMode/native runs. The details, including the effect-by-effect analysis, are in `reports/card_flow_20261016/effect_candidates_author_report.md`.
